raw_response:
This sorghum plot is small but important for my family's food. The land here in Tigray is tired, so I put some manure from my animals on it before the rains, and I will buy a little DAP and urea from the cooperative if the price is not too high this year. I keep my own sorghum seed from last harvest — the local variety handles our dry spells better than what the extension people bring. I depend on the rains; I have no pump or canal, and for weeding my wife and older children will help me, but I may call two neighbors for a few days when the weeds get ahead of us.
